newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican businessmen play down U.S. drug war debate.
newsitem.headline: Mexican businessmen play down U.S. drug war debate.

text.p: Mexican bankers and businessmen on Friday played down the continuing battle over President Clinton's decision to certify Mexico as an ally of the U.S. in the war on drugs.
Meeting in this pristine beach resort for the 60th annual bankers convention, business leaders shrugged off the possibility that the U.S. Congress would vote to reverse Clinton's decision.

"We have full confidence in Mexico. I am sure that nothing is going to happen," Hector Larios Santillan, chairman of the Business Coordinating Council, one of Mexico's top umbrella business groups, told reporters.

A U.S. House of Representatives committee voted Thursday to overturn Clinton's finding last week that Mexico is fully cooperating in the war on drugs. But the panel voted to waive the imposition of sanctions against Mexico.
The 27-5 vote to send the measure to the full House for action was the first step toward overturning Clinton's ratification of Mexico's anti-drug efforts.
"Certification or decertification is not worth getting all hot and bothered about," said Antonio Del Valle Ruiz, the soon-to-be-elected chairman of the Association of Bankers.

"Fortunately, the economic position of Mexico is fine, we are promoting internal savings, and foreign inflows are not only coming from the United States but also from Europe and Japan," said Del Valle, who will be officially elected to the post during the convention.

Ricardo Guajardo, chairman of Mexico's second largest financial company Grupo Financiero Bancomer, said he did not expect the certification debate to have a major impact on Mexican financial markets, although he recognized the financial sector should be attentive to events.

"I do not give it that much importance and I do not believe that this type of event is a very serious problem, (but) it can cause friction in the intense relation that Mexico and the United States have," he said.
